suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause records only Columbia Capital Management's acceptance of the engagement and its obligation to perform, without imposing any express corresponding commitment on the City — most critically, the City's obligation to compensate Columbia Capital Management for those services. This asymmetry means that the foundational engagement clause, standing alone, binds Columbia Capital Management to perform while leaving the City's core reciprocal duty unacknowledged at the point of engagement, which could weaken Columbia Capital Management's position if a payment dispute arises and the City contests the basis of its payment obligation. A minimal bilateral acknowledgment referencing the City's obligation to compensate Columbia Capital Management corrects this imbalance without altering the structure of the clause.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement and Consultant accepts that engagement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement, and the City agrees to compensate Consultant for such services as set forth in this Agreement, and Consultant accepts that engagement.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to scope creep risk because it contains no express statement that services not set out in Exhibit A are outside the scope of the Contract Services, allowing the City to argue that unlisted work is implicitly captured within the agreed engagement without additional compensation. The change control mechanism compounds this risk by being unilateral: it activates only "at the City's request," meaning Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual right to initiate a written scope adjustment and must absorb any disputed boundary between in-scope and out-of-scope work without a triggering mechanism of its own. Left unaddressed, this combination creates a pathway for the City to demand additional performance from Columbia Capital Management while contesting entitlement to supplemental compensation.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Any services not expressly set forth in Exhibit A are outside the scope of the Contract Services. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement, and either Party may propose a change to the scope of the Contract Services. Upon such request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional or changed work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of such work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: Section 3 as drafted is a bare payment placeholder that exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant financial risk: it establishes no invoicing process, no payment due date, no mechanism for handling disputed invoices, no late-payment remedy, and no treatment of expenses, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no contractual basis to enforce timely payment or recover interest on overdue amounts. The sole reference to Exhibit A for fee amounts, without specifying the fee basis or whether fees are fixed or subject to adjustment, creates further uncertainty should a dispute arise over the scope of compensable Contract Services. Without a payment due date and a late-payment interest provision, the City faces no financial consequence for delayed payment, directly undermining Columbia Capital Management's cash flow position throughout the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City may terminate this Agreement for "cause" with the same sixty (60) days' notice used for a convenience termination, without any obligation to identify the alleged breach or afford Columbia Capital Management an opportunity to remedy it. This exposes Columbia Capital Management to the reputational and financial consequences of a for-cause termination — which may trigger downstream rights or affect future engagements — without any procedural safeguard against an erroneous or disputed allegation. The absence of a cure period also means that a minor, readily correctable performance issue could be weaponized to terminate the relationship on a "cause" basis rather than for convenience, with no practical distinction in outcome for Columbia Capital Management. Additionally, while sixty (60) days' notice is stated, the clause does not expressly fix the effective date of termination by reference to delivery of that notice, creating potential ambiguity about when Columbia Capital Management's obligations and payment entitlements cease.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant, effective sixty (60) days following delivery of such notice. The City may terminate this Agreement for cause upon written notice to Consultant specifying the material breach in reasonable detail, provided that Consultant shall have thirty (30) days following delivery of such notice to cure the identified breach, and termination for cause shall not take effect if Consultant cures the breach within that period. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the effective date of termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' written notice, effective sixty (60) days following delivery of such notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Compliance with Laws clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant legal and financial risk in four respects: it contains no express reference to anti-bribery, anti-corruption, or supply-chain labor standards (including prohibitions on forced and child labor), leaving Columbia Capital Management's compliance posture undefined against those regulatory requirements; it imposes no mutual notification obligation, meaning the City need not alert Columbia Capital Management to a legal breach that could directly affect performance or Columbia Capital Management's own regulatory standing; and it is silent on who bears the incremental cost of a change in law occurring after engagement, which could require Columbia Capital Management to absorb unforeseen compliance costs with no recourse. The absence of these protections, combined with the existing unilateral indemnification running solely in favor of the City, leaves Columbia Capital Management with disproportionate and open-ended exposure under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause limits Consultant's compliance obligations exclusively to Kansas-specific anti-discrimination statutes, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed where Consultant breaches anti-corruption laws, engages in forced or child labor practices, or violates any other law material to performance of this Agreement. There is no obligation on Consultant to notify Columbia Capital Management of such a breach, meaning Columbia Capital Management could unknowingly remain in a relationship with a non-compliant counterparty and face reputational, regulatory, or financial consequences as a result. These omissions are material given that Columbia Capital Management, as a capital management firm, is likely subject to heightened regulatory scrutiny and counterparty conduct standards. The clause requires expansion to address all applicable laws, anti-bribery obligations, supply-chain labor standards, and a breach-notification requirement in favor of Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Compliance with Laws; Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.), and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant shall not engage in any act of bribery or corruption in connection with this Agreement, shall take commercially reasonable steps to prevent forced labor and human trafficking in its supply chain, and shall promptly notify Columbia Capital Management in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of applicable law that affects the performance of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts the Consultant's insurance maintenance obligation to "throughout the duration of this Agreement" only, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to uninsured claims arising from services performed under this Agreement but asserted after its expiration or termination — a material risk in professional services engagements where errors, omissions, or other liabilities frequently surface well beyond contract close. Equally significant, the clause contains no statement that the procurement or maintenance of insurance does not limit or cap the Consultant's total liability, creating a credible argument by the Consultant that its policy limits define the ceiling of its financial exposure to Columbia Capital Management. This gap could materially impair Columbia Capital Management's ability to recover damages exceeding those limits, particularly for significant professional liability or indemnification claims.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of two (2) years following the expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The procurement and maintenance of insurance as required herein shall not be construed to limit or otherwise affect Consultant's liability to the City under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 9 exposes Columbia Capital Management to three compounding risks: first, the opening "without in any way limiting" language, combined with the absence of any express reference to the Agreement's limitation of liability provisions, could be read to place this indemnity obligation entirely outside any liability cap that may otherwise protect Columbia Capital Management; second, the claims-handling mechanism is one-sided, requiring only that Columbia Capital Management give notice to the City but imposing no obligation on the City to cooperate with the defense or to allow Columbia Capital Management to control the defense and approve settlements; and third, the absence of any mitigation obligation on the City as the indemnified party means the City faces no requirement to take reasonable steps to limit its losses, leaving Columbia Capital Management potentially exposed to inflated or avoidable claims. These gaps, taken together, could result in uncapped, uncontrolled, and uninhibited indemnity exposure for Columbia Capital Management across the life of the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, and subject to any limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. Consultant shall have the right to control the defense and settlement of any claim subject to this provision, provided that any settlement that imposes obligations on the City shall require the City's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. The City shall cooperate with Consultant in connection with any such defense and shall take reasonable steps to mitigate its losses. Consultant shall give the City prompt written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.

suggestions.reason: The savings clause preserving duties "as imposed by law" is undefined and open-ended, meaning that despite the no-third-party-beneficiary restriction, the clause expressly leaves intact every statutory and common law obligation either party owes to third parties without qualification or ceiling. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates a material financial risk: a third party who cannot sue under the Agreement could nonetheless argue that this clause confirms the survival of unlimited tort, statutory, or regulatory duties owed by Columbia Capital Management, potentially bypassing any liability cap negotiated elsewhere in the Agreement. The phrase "as imposed by law" is sufficiently indeterminate that two courts could read it to preserve materially different categories of third-party liability, leaving Columbia Capital Management's exposure scope unresolved at the moment a claim arises. Anchoring the savings clause to "applicable law" and expressly subordinating preserved duties to the Agreement's limitation of liability provisions closes this gap.
suggestions.original_text: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by applicable law, subject in all respects to the limitations of liability set forth in this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 11 exposes Columbia Capital Management to serious legal and financial risk on multiple fronts. The clause specifies no governing law and no designated forum, meaning either party is "free to take such steps as it deems necessary," which could allow the City to initiate proceedings in an inconvenient or hostile jurisdiction while leaving Columbia Capital Management without a predictable dispute resolution framework. The negotiation obligation uses the precatory "should" rather than a binding obligation and contains no timeframe, rendering it unenforceable as a condition precedent to litigation. Most critically, the performance-continuation obligation runs only against the Consultant, meaning Columbia Capital Management must keep performing even if the City withholds payment or commits a material breach, an entirely one-sided allocation of risk that would strip Columbia Capital Management of its most valuable practical leverage in any dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: The original paragraph contains only a single anti-collusion representation regarding pricing, leaving Columbia Capital Management entirely unprotected on the most commercially material aspects of the engagement: the standard to which Services will be performed, compliance with applicable laws, freedom from third-party intellectual property infringement, the remedy available upon breach, and the period during which any warranty applies. Without a performance standard, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to demand re-performance or a fee refund if Services are delivered deficiently, and the absence of a non-infringement warranty directly exposes Columbia Capital Management to uncapped third-party IP liability arising from the provider's work product. These cumulative gaps leave Columbia Capital Management without enforceable recourse across the full scope of the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Each party further represents and warrants that it shall comply with all applicable laws in connection with this Agreement. Provider additionally represents and warrants that: (i) the Services shall be performed with the professional skill and care reasonably expected of a qualified provider in the relevant field; (ii) the Services and all deliverables shall not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights; and (iii) in the event of a breach of the foregoing warranties, Provider shall, at Columbia Capital Management's election, promptly re-perform the non-conforming Services at no additional charge or refund the fees paid for such non-conforming Services. The warranties set forth in this Section shall apply during the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months following completion of the relevant Services.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation in this paragraph runs solely in favor of the engagement — only Consultant warrants its power and authority to execute and perform the Agreement — but no corresponding representation is made by Columbia Capital Management. This asymmetry exposes Columbia Capital Management to a material enforceability risk: if a dispute arises, the absence of a mutual authority representation means Consultant could challenge whether Columbia Capital Management was duly authorized to enter the Agreement, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce its contractual rights and remedies. A market-standard professional services agreement requires both parties to represent their respective authority, and the gap here should be remedied to place both parties on equal footing.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents that it has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement, and that the individuals who have signed this Agreement on its behalf have the legal power, right, and authority to make this Agreement and to bind such party.

suggestions.reason: The quality warranties in this Section rely entirely on undefined and subjective standards — "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field," "state of the art procedures and techniques," and "ready comprehension of the required subject matter" — none of which are defined in the Agreement or anchored to any objective, ascertainable benchmark, leaving each standard open to dispute if Columbia Capital Management seeks to enforce them. As a result, if Consultant delivers substandard work, Consultant can plausibly argue that whatever it delivered satisfied a loosely interpreted industry norm, depriving Columbia Capital Management of a clear evidentiary basis to establish breach. Further, while the clause imposes warranties on Consultant, it provides Columbia Capital Management with no express remedy — such as re-performance — if those warranties are breached, reducing them to declarations of intent rather than enforceable contractual protections.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to or exceed the professional standards generally accepted in the relevant industry at the time of performance. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of current, industry-accepted procedures and techniques applicable to the Services. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and shall possess sufficient knowledge and expertise in the required subject matter to provide these services. In the event of a breach of any warranty in this Section, Columbia Capital Management shall be entitled to require Consultant to re-perform the non-conforming work promptly and at no additional cost to Columbia Capital Management.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the assignment restriction is entirely one-sided: only the Consultant (Columbia Capital Management) requires the City's consent to assign, while the City faces no corresponding restriction and may freely transfer this Agreement to any third party without Columbia Capital Management's approval. The City's consent right is also unconstrained — no reasonableness standard or response period applies — meaning the City could withhold or delay consent arbitrarily to gain commercial leverage over Columbia Capital Management. The clause further contains no affiliate or corporate reorganization carve-out, exposing Columbia Capital Management to default risk upon an internal restructuring, and it is silent on change of control, continuing liability of the assignor, and any termination right triggered by an unwanted change of control of the City.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either party may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its business or assets without consent, and the assigning party shall remain liable for all obligations accrued prior to such assignment. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice if the other party undergoes a change of control. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the permitted successors and assigns of each party.

suggestions.reason: The Notices clause sets out Columbia Capital Management's contact details but contains no mechanism for either party to update those details during the term of the Agreement. Without such a mechanism, Columbia Capital Management has no clear contractual basis to substitute a new address, contact, or representative if its circumstances change, and any notice sent to a stale address could be deemed validly delivered, potentially causing Columbia Capital Management to miss time-sensitive communications such as termination notices or indemnity claims. Adding a written-notice amendment procedure protects Columbia Capital Management's ability to maintain current and effective notice coordinates throughout the Agreement's term.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice details by providing written notice of such change to the other party, which change shall be effective five (5) Business Days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 16 leaves three material gaps that expose Columbia Capital Management to legal and financial risk. First, the clause is silent on who controls the manner and means of performance, which undermines Columbia Capital Management's independent contractor status and could invite the City to assert employment-classification arguments or exercise operational control over Columbia Capital Management's work. Second, the tax and withholdings obligation runs only against Consultant, without any corresponding obligation on the City for its own personnel's costs and benefits, creating an asymmetric allocation that could expose Columbia Capital Management to claims if the City's own personnel costs are disputed. Third, the absence of a mutual non-authority statement means there is no express bar preventing either party from purporting to bind the other, leaving Columbia Capital Management potentially exposed to unauthorized commitments made by City personnel.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor, and Consultant shall control the manner and means by which it performs the Services hereunder. Each party shall be responsible for and pay all compensation, benefits, taxes, and withholdings required by law with respect to its own personnel; provided that Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability arising from Consultant's failure to satisfy such obligations with respect to Consultant's personnel. Neither party shall have authority to bind the other party to any obligation, contract, or commitment. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 17 addresses only the Kansas Cash-Basis Law appropriation mechanism and is silent on anti-bribery and corruption obligations, modern slavery and forced labor prohibitions, the obligation to notify the counterparty of a material legal breach, and the allocation of costs when applicable law changes — all of which expose Columbia Capital Management to unmitigated compliance risk on each of those fronts. The City's unfettered "sole discretion" non-appropriation right, with no notice obligation whatsoever, further prejudices Columbia Capital Management by permitting abrupt termination without any wind-down notice, leaving Columbia Capital Management unable to cease work and mitigate costs in an orderly manner. The absence of a change-in-law cost allocation is particularly acute because regulatory change could increase Columbia Capital Management's service delivery costs mid-engagement with no contractual basis for cost recovery or relief.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended, and all other applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including those governing anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and the prohibition of forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects performance of this Agreement. Each party shall bear its own costs of complying with any change in applicable law, except that Columbia Capital Management may adjust its fees upon reasonable written notice to the extent a change in law materially increases its cost of performance. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, the City shall provide Columbia Capital Management with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and the parties shall thereafter be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The undefined term "legal actions" creates genuine ambiguity about whether this exclusive venue provision covers all proceedings, including emergency injunctive relief, leaving Columbia Capital Management potentially unable to seek urgent remedies in a convenient or appropriate court. The clause also restricts venue to a single state court without preserving access to federal courts in Kansas, which may be the proper or preferred forum for certain disputes, and that limitation could disproportionately burden Columbia Capital Management depending on the nature or complexity of a claim. As drafted, the provision binds both parties equally in name but in practice may impose greater litigation cost and logistical disadvantage on Columbia Capital Management if the counterparty is locally situated in Johnson County, Kansas.
suggestions.original_text: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions or proceedings arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be the state or federal courts in Johnson County, Kansas; provided that either party may seek injunctive or equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.

suggestions.reason: The current provision does nothing beyond selecting Kansas law, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed on five material fronts: there is no designated forum, meaning a counterparty could initiate proceedings in any court it chooses; there are no mandatory pre-dispute escalation steps, removing the opportunity for cost-effective early resolution; there is no mutual submission to an exclusive jurisdiction, so Columbia Capital Management cannot reliably enforce a forum selection against the counterparty; there is no carve-out preserving the right to seek urgent injunctive or equitable relief; and there is no obligation on either party to continue performing during a live dispute, creating leverage for the counterparty to suspend Services and cause operational harm to Columbia Capital Management. These omissions collectively leave Columbia Capital Management without a predictable, enforceable dispute resolution framework under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.

suggestions.reason: The second sentence of Section 21 creates a material interpretive risk for Columbia Capital Management by declaring that capitalization has no legal bearing on the interpretation of any term across the Agreement. This directly contradicts the Agreement's definitional architecture, under which capitalized terms such as "Services," "Confidential Information," and "Deliverables" carry specific, negotiated meanings that protect Columbia Capital Management's rights and limit counterparty obligations. A counterparty could invoke this clause to argue that a capitalized Defined Term should be read in its ordinary, uncapitalized sense, potentially stripping Columbia Capital Management of key contractual protections in a dispute. The clause as drafted creates genuine ambiguity that a court could resolve against Columbia Capital Management, particularly in provisions governing scope of services, liability, and confidentiality.
suggestions.original_text: Section 21. Descriptive Headings and Capitalization. The descriptive headings of the provisions of this Agreement are formulated and used only for convenience and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning and construction of any such provision. Some terms are capitalized throughout the Agreement, but use of or failure to use capitals shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation of such terms.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 21. Descriptive Headings and Capitalization. The descriptive headings of the provisions of this Agreement are formulated and used only for convenience and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning and construction of any such provision. Some terms are capitalized throughout the Agreement, but use of or failure to use capitals shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation of such terms, except that any term expressly defined in this Agreement shall retain its defined meaning when used in capitalized form.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is legally uncertain in a way that creates material risk for Columbia Capital Management: it neither identifies which party determines the content of the reformed provision nor limits reformation to the minimum change necessary, meaning a counterparty could argue that an invalid provision has been automatically rewritten in a manner that expands its own rights or narrows Columbia Capital Management's protections without Columbia Capital Management's consent or court approval. The word "automatically" removes any procedural safeguard—such as mutual written agreement or judicial determination—that would otherwise protect Columbia Capital Management from an adverse unilateral reinterpretation. Additionally, "all applicable legal requirements" is an undefined and open-ended standard that offers no objective benchmark against which any reformed provision could be assessed, leaving the operative effect of this clause genuinely indeterminate.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable under applicable law, as mutually agreed in writing by the parties or, failing such agreement, as determined by a court of competent jurisdiction, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by such modification, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: Section 23 addresses non-waiver of future rights arising from the same term or provision, but it does not state that a waiver of one breach or right leaves all other breaches and rights unaffected. Without this element, a counterparty could argue that Columbia Capital Management's decision to waive a specific breach or right under one provision creates an implied precedent bearing on separate provisions or distinct breaches, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce unrelated or subsequent obligations selectively. This gap is particularly relevant where Columbia Capital Management may need to accommodate a counterparty on one obligation (e.g., a delivery timeline) without prejudicing its independent right to enforce payment, confidentiality, or intellectual property obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any breach of any term or provision of this Agreement shall be construed as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach, or of any other term, provision, option, right, or remedy. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.

suggestions.reason: The reference to "documents incorporated by reference" is undefined and unanchored—no Schedule, Exhibit, or list identifies which documents qualify—exposing Columbia Capital Management to counterparty arguments that pre-contractual proposals, term sheets, or correspondence have been incorporated and can be used to vary the Agreement's terms. Separately, limiting the merger clause's scope to "professional services set forth herein" rather than the broader and legally standard "subject matter hereof" creates a gap through which a counterparty could contend that provisions not strictly characterized as professional services—such as confidentiality, intellectual property ownership, or indemnification—fall outside the clause's reach, permitting extrinsic evidence to be introduced against Columbia Capital Management's interests in any dispute. Both defects undermine the certainty and finality that an integration clause is designed to provide.
suggestions.original_text: Section 24. Merger. This Agreement and the documents incorporated by reference constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the professional services set forth herein. There are no verbal understandings, agreements, representations or warranties between the parties that are not expressly set forth herein. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties, both written and oral.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 24. Merger. This Agreement and the Schedules and Exhibits attached hereto and expressly incorporated herein constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. There are no verbal understandings, agreements, representations or warranties between the parties that are not expressly set forth herein. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties, both written and oral.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, Section 25 exclusively restricts the binding effect of verbal statements made by the City's officials and representatives, while imposing no equivalent limitation on verbal statements attributable to Columbia Capital Management's own representatives — exposing Columbia Capital Management to the risk that an informal oral communication by one of its personnel could be argued to modify or supplement the Agreement's written terms. The phrase "any and every official or other representative of the City" is also undefined and subject to dispute, leaving open the question of whose statements qualify, which could be used against Columbia Capital Management in any disagreement about the scope of contracted services or approved changes. Making the provision mutual and replacing the undefined class description with "representative of either party" corrects both the asymmetry and the definitional gap without altering the clause's core integration purpose.
suggestions.original_text: Section 25. Verbal Statements Not Binding. It is understood and agreed that the written terms and provisions of this Agreement supersede all verbal statements of any and every official or other representative of the City, and such statements shall not be effective or be construed as entering into, or forming a part of, or altering in any way whatsoever, this written Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 25. Verbal Statements Not Binding. It is understood and agreed that the written terms and provisions of this Agreement supersede all verbal statements of any representative of either party, and such statements shall not be effective or be construed as entering into, or forming a part of, or altering in any way whatsoever, this written Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 26 does not require that amendments be signed by authorized representatives, exposing Columbia Capital Management to the risk that an amendment could be executed by a person lacking actual authority and later disputed or repudiated by the counterparty. The clause also does not expressly extend to schedules and exhibits, which in a Professional Services Agreement commonly contain scope, pricing, and deliverable terms of significant commercial importance to Columbia Capital Management. The absence of any prohibition on oral or conduct-based modification creates further risk that a counterparty could assert that correspondence, course of dealing, or informal exchanges altered Columbia Capital Management's contractual rights without a formal written instrument.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including all schedules and exhibits, may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by a duly authorized representative of each party. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or conduct shall constitute or operate as an amendment to this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the survival clause identifies only the Consultant's obligations under Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), while omitting express survival of provisions that directly protect Columbia Capital Management, such as confidentiality and work product ownership — leaving those critical protections potentially extinguishable upon termination. The vague catch-all — "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination" — is sufficiently indefinite that a court or arbitrator could apply it to impose unanticipated continuing obligations on Columbia Capital Management, exposing the firm to arguments that its own payment, indemnification, or other obligations persist without limit. Furthermore, by identifying the Consultant's obligations without expressly preserving Columbia Capital Management's corresponding rights to enforce them post-termination, the clause creates a structural asymmetry that a counterparty could exploit to resist post-termination claims. The suggested fix enumerates Columbia Capital Management's key protective provisions alongside the Consultant's obligations, adds Columbia Capital Management's corresponding rights, and anchors the catch-all to provisions that expressly provide for survival, eliminating the operative ambiguity.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8), Indemnification (Section 9), Confidentiality, and Work Product ownership, together with Columbia Capital Management's corresponding rights under those provisions, shall survive the termination of this Agreement, as shall any other provisions that expressly provide for survival or that by their express written terms are intended to survive termination.

suggestions.reason: The compliance covenant imposed on Columbia Capital Management through the phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is undefined, unbounded, and potentially unlimited in scope, exposing Columbia Capital Management to breach of contract liability for any failure to comply with any law across any conceivable legal framework — a standard no reasonable counterparty counsel would accept and no court could apply with certainty. The absence of a materiality qualifier compounds this exposure, meaning a technical or immaterial regulatory deviation could be characterised as a breach of the Agreement, triggering remedies against Columbia Capital Management with no proportionality check. Additionally, the clause imposes compliance obligations exclusively on Columbia Capital Management while placing no corresponding obligation on the City to cooperate, provide accurate information, or fulfill its own duties in connection with the Accounts. These defects should be addressed before execution, as the appointment clause is foundational and cross-references to any indemnification or termination provisions in the Agreement may amplify Columbia Capital Management's exposure under the current formulation.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in all material respects in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable laws and regulations governing the provision of investment advisory services. The City shall provide Consultant with reasonable cooperation and timely access to all information and documentation reasonably necessary for Consultant to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a fiduciary duty on Consultant using language that mirrors ERISA's prudent-person standard, but the phrases "enterprise of like character and with like aims" are entirely undefined and unanchored within the Agreement, leaving the operative benchmark open to dispute. If Consultant were to breach its fiduciary obligations, it could invoke a comparator enterprise with materially lower standards than the investment management mandate actually entrusted to Consultant under this Agreement, diluting the protection Columbia Capital Management bargained for. Additionally, the clause is structurally one-sided: it articulates Consultant's duty but provides no express remedy or reference to Consultant's accountability to Columbia Capital Management upon a breach of that standard, leaving Columbia Capital Management to rely solely on general contract law remedies rather than the heightened standard the clause purports to establish.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent investment professional acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an investment management enterprise of like character and with investment objectives similar to those described in this Agreement. Any failure by Consultant to satisfy this standard of care shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement for which Columbia Capital Management shall be entitled to pursue all available remedies.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the scope of services imposed on Columbia Capital Management is entirely open-ended: the catch-all obligation to respond to "ad hoc reporting and other routine requests" creates an unbounded service obligation with no frequency cap, materiality threshold, or mechanism to treat out-of-scope demands as additional compensable work. This exposes Columbia Capital Management to unlimited service creep at the City's discretion without any corresponding reciprocal commitment from the City to provide timely, accurate information necessary for Columbia Capital Management to perform. Left unaddressed, the City could characterize virtually any request as "routine," effectively expanding Columbia Capital Management's contracted workload without additional compensation or scope adjustment.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant’s scope of services shall include:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant's scope of services shall include: Providing recommendations; Implementing an investment strategy; Complying with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675 et seq.; Monitoring and marking-to-market the collateral; Selecting investment securities; Providing periodic portfolio reporting; Working with the city attorney; and Providing the City with general market information and reasonably requested ad hoc reporting, provided that requests materially exceeding the ordinary scope of services described herein shall be subject to mutual written agreement on additional compensation. The City shall provide Columbia Capital Management with timely access to all information and materials reasonably necessary for Columbia Capital Management to perform the foregoing services.

suggestions.reason: The term "periodic" is wholly undefined and creates material operational and legal exposure for Columbia Capital Management, as the City could contend at any time that reporting frequency is insufficient and assert a breach of the Agreement. Without an objective frequency standard anchored to a defined interval, Columbia Capital Management has no clear benchmark against which its performance can be measured or defended, leaving the scope of this ongoing delivery obligation vulnerable to unilateral reinterpretation by the City. This ambiguity is particularly prejudicial to Columbia Capital Management because the reporting obligation runs continuously throughout the term, meaning the risk of a disputed breach is recurring and cumulative.
suggestions.original_text: Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing quarterly portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to two compounding risks. First, the City retains unilateral authority to impose new written investment policy objectives and guidelines "from time to time" with no advance notice period, meaning Columbia Capital Management could be held in breach of guidelines it had no reasonable opportunity to operationalize — creating open-ended liability for prior compliant transactions that post-dated a guideline change. Second, the obligation to achieve "best execution" is left undefined within the clause and apparently nowhere else in the Agreement, creating an ambiguous performance standard against which Columbia Capital Management's execution decisions could be measured retroactively and arbitrarily. Together, these provisions leave Columbia Capital Management operating under a shifting and undefined compliance framework with no corresponding protection for transactions executed in good faith under the guidelines and standards then in effect.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City upon not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice, and Consultant shall not be liable for any transactions executed in conformity with the written investment policy objectives and guidelines then in effect at the time of execution. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution as defined under applicable federal and state securities laws and regulations, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" imposes no objectively enforceable deadline on the City, meaning Columbia Capital Management cannot establish a breach even if critical account data is withheld for weeks, directly undermining its ability to execute and monitor the investment plan. Without a definite reporting period, the City retains de facto discretion over when it performs this foundational information obligation, exposing Columbia Capital Management to operational gaps, delayed investment decisions, and potential liability for underperformance attributable to the City's own tardiness. A specific post-period deadline replaces the vague standard with an objectively assessable trigger that Columbia Capital Management can enforce.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts within five (5) Business Days following the end of each calendar month.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "properly determine required liquidity" introduces an undefined performance standard against which Columbia Capital Management's work could be measured, creating exposure to the City disputing whether Columbia Capital Management's liquidity analysis met an unspecified threshold of correctness. Similarly, "to effect the investment plan" references an instrument that is not defined in this clause or identified elsewhere in the Agreement, leaving the scope and purpose of the City's disclosure obligation ambiguous and contestable. Left unaddressed, these undefined terms could allow the City to claim that Columbia Capital Management failed to perform adequately by reference to standards Columbia Capital Management had no opportunity to review or confirm at the time of engagement. Anchoring both concepts to the Agreement's existing framework removes that uncertainty and protects Columbia Capital Management from unfounded performance challenges.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to determine the liquidity levels required to implement the investment objectives under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City's obligation to respond to fund transfer requests is qualified only by "reasonable notice," with no defined notice period and no deadline by which the City must actually act. This creates a material operational risk for Columbia Capital Management: if the City delays indefinitely in executing wire transfers, Columbia Capital Management may be unable to implement the investment plan on time, yet could face liability for investment underperformance caused entirely by the City's inaction. The absence of a minimum notice standard and a response deadline leaves the trigger condition and the City's corresponding duty unenforceable against an objective benchmark, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to manage the City's portfolio effectively.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with no less than one (1) Business Day's prior written notice, respond within one (1) Business Day to Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City's obligation to instruct the Custodian is conditioned entirely on receipt of "copies of confirmations" from Consultant, but neither the form nor content of those confirmations is defined anywhere in the clause, leaving the City room to dispute whether a given communication from Columbia Capital Management satisfies the condition and thereby delay or refuse Custodian instruction. More critically, the clause contains no timeframe within which the City must act after receiving confirmations from Columbia Capital Management, creating material settlement risk: if the City delays instructing the Custodian, trades executed by Columbia Capital Management could fail to settle on time, exposing Columbia Capital Management to counterparty claims, failed-trade penalties, and reputational harm that may in turn be attributed to Columbia Capital Management's performance under this Agreement. The absence of a clear temporal trigger and an objective definition of "confirmations" gives the City unilateral latitude to stall settlement without contractual consequence.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian, within one (1) Business Day of receiving written trade confirmations from Consultant, to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with such written trade confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted imposes no obligation on Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to Columbia Capital Management, leaving the City entirely dependent on Consultant's self-administered internal policy rather than any enforceable contractual right to be informed. This is a material gap: without a mandatory disclosure obligation, Columbia Capital Management cannot evaluate whether a conflict is adversely affecting its Accounts, cannot seek independent advice, and has no contractual basis to demand remediation. Additionally, the conflict-avoidance commitment is framed as a unilateral "policy" rather than a binding contractual duty, which means Consultant could deviate from it without being in breach of this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, Consultant shall not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf of an investing client, nor purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. Consultant shall promptly disclose to the City in writing any actual or potential conflict of interest arising from its concurrent representation of an Issuer Client that may affect the City's Accounts. This obligation serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The City's unfettered right to amend Schedule X "at any time" with nothing more than unspecified "notice provided to Consultant" exposes Columbia Capital Management to serious operational and legal risk: without a minimum advance notice period, Columbia Capital Management could receive binding instructions from newly authorized individuals before it has had a reasonable opportunity to verify credentials or update its internal controls, and could face liability for acting on a superseded authorized-persons list. Additionally, the phrase "aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City" is insufficiently precise — the absence of any objective standard for what constitutes non-identification leaves Columbia Capital Management vulnerable to a City claim that published performance data impermissibly disclosed the City's identity, even where Columbia Capital Management acted in good faith.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to Consultant; Consultant shall not be liable for acts taken in reliance on the then-current Schedule X prior to Consultant's receipt of any such written amendment. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City by name or in any manner that would reasonably permit identification of the City.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Management Fees clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant collection risk: it states no payment due date, provides no mechanism for the paying party to dispute an invoice, imposes no consequence for late payment, and contains no notice period for fee adjustments, leaving the fee effectively locked indefinitely with no recourse if the counterparty delays or withholds payment. The "sole compensation" language, taken in isolation, could also be construed to bar Columbia Capital Management from recovering pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses incurred in performing the advisory services. These omissions collectively undermine Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce timely payment and adjust its fee structure over the life of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000.
