Invoices shall be issued within fifteen (15) days following the close of each quarter and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Any disputed portion of an invoice shall be notified in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, with undisputed amounts remaining due and payable on the original due date; undisputed amounts not paid when due shall accrue interest at 1.5% per month from the due date until paid. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Consultant may adjust the fee schedule upon not less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, excluding pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause imposes a unilateral disclosure obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management as Consultant, while placing no corresponding notice obligation on the City regarding events that may equally affect the Accounts or Columbia Capital Management's ability to perform its obligations. This asymmetry leaves Columbia Capital Management operationally exposed: if the City becomes aware of a material event pertaining to the Accounts but has no contractual duty to disclose it, Columbia Capital Management may be left without information critical to managing those Accounts and could face liability for decisions made in ignorance. The undefined scope of "certain events" further compounds this risk, as it creates ambiguity about whether Columbia Capital Management has fully discharged its notice obligation, potentially exposing it to breach claims by the City.
suggestions.original_text: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City, and the City shall provide written notice to Consultant, regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of the notifying party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted is grammatically defective — the phrase "shall be immediately up the occurrence" omits the operative verb and the word "upon," rendering the entire notice obligation unenforceable on its face. Even if a court were to supply the missing words by inference, the standard "immediately" imposes an undefined and subjective obligation that could expose Columbia Capital Management to a claim of breach if notice is delivered even a matter of hours after an event occurs. This ambiguity creates material legal and operational risk for Columbia Capital Management, particularly where the triggering events may require internal assessment before notice can responsibly be given. The provision must be corrected to include both the operative verb and a definite, objective time period.
suggestions.original_text: Written notice shall be immediately up the occurrence of any of the following events:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Written notice shall be provided within two (2) Business Days following the occurrence of any of the following events:

suggestions.reason: The phrase "material adverse change to Consultant's financial condition or status" is undefined in the Agreement, leaving Consultant with broad discretion to characterize whether a triggering event is sufficiently "material" or "adverse" to warrant notice to Columbia Capital Management. This ambiguity creates a material operational and financial risk for Columbia Capital Management: if Consultant delays or withholds notice by asserting a deterioration in its finances does not meet the undefined threshold, Columbia Capital Management may be unable to take protective action — such as engaging a replacement consultant or safeguarding work product — before the Consultant's ability to perform is compromised. Anchoring the trigger to an objective standard tied to Consultant's capacity to perform is necessary to make the notice obligation enforceable and commercially meaningful.
suggestions.original_text: A material adverse change to Consultant’s financial condition or status;
suggestions.suggested_fix: A material adverse change to Consultant's financial condition or status, meaning any event or circumstance that would reasonably be expected to impair Consultant's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement;

suggestions.reason: The term "Custodian" is used without definition anywhere in this clause or, apparently, the broader Agreement, creating a dispute risk for Columbia Capital Management as to which entity the City is obligated to direct and whether that direction has validly occurred. More critically, the phrase "no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies" is ambiguous in scope: a counterparty could argue it merely relieves Columbia Capital Management of a duty to cast votes while leaving intact a broader obligation under its investment advisory mandate to provide proxy voting recommendations or guidance, thereby exposing Columbia Capital Management to liability for failing to do so. Clarifying "Custodian" by reference to its function and specifying that Columbia Capital Management's exclusion covers both any duty to act and any liability for outcomes will close these interpretive gaps and protect Columbia Capital Management from claims arising out of proxy voting decisions it does not control.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the custodian appointed to hold the City's investment assets (the "Custodian") in voting of all proxies, and Consultant shall have no duty to vote, direct the voting of, or provide recommendations with respect to any proxies, and no liability for any proxy voting outcomes.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to material gaps in its contractual protections: it captures only registration status under the Consultants Act and contains no general warranty of legal compliance, no representation that the Consultant's services are free from third-party intellectual property infringement, and no defined remedy if any of these warranties are breached. Without a law-compliance warranty, Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual basis to claim breach if the Consultant violates other applicable laws during performance; without an IP non-infringement warranty, Columbia Capital Management bears the risk of third-party infringement claims arising from services it has procured and paid for. The absence of a stated remedy for breach of warranty leaves Columbia Capital Management without a clear contractual right to re-performance or a fee refund, forcing it to rely solely on general damages principles to seek relief.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act") and complies with all applicable laws and regulations in performing this Agreement; (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; and (iv) warrants that the services provided hereunder do not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights. Upon breach of any of the foregoing warranties, Consultant shall, at the City's election, re-perform the affected services at no additional cost or refund the fees paid for such non-conforming services.

suggestions.reason: The provision identifies the Consultant as a fiduciary but does not articulate the standard of skill, care, or diligence to which that fiduciary duty is anchored, leaving Columbia Capital Management without an objective performance benchmark against which to measure and enforce the Consultant's conduct in managing its assets. Equally, the obligation contains no temporal scope, creating ambiguity as to whether the fiduciary duty applies at inception of the engagement, throughout the Term, or at some other point, which undermines Columbia Capital Management's ability to pursue a claim for fiduciary breach tied to a defined period of underperformance. If left unaddressed, the Consultant could argue that its fiduciary status alone, absent a stated standard, imposes only the most general duty, limiting Columbia Capital Management's remedies.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant is, throughout the Term, a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement and shall perform such management obligations with the skill, care, and diligence of a professional investment adviser;

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is entirely unilateral: only the Consultant warrants that it is duly authorized and empowered to enter into and perform this Agreement, while Columbia Capital Management makes no corresponding representation. This creates an enforcement asymmetry that exposes Columbia Capital Management to a challenge by the Consultant that the Agreement is unenforceable on the basis that Columbia Capital Management itself lacked requisite authority at signing, without Columbia Capital Management having the reciprocal protection of holding the Consultant to a mutual admission. As a matter of market-standard practice in professional services agreements, authority representations are made by both contracting parties, and the absence of a mutual obligation leaves a material gap in the Agreement's foundational enforceability framework.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
